correctness.rationale: Define U_k as number of the two species appearing in exactly one of k uniformly sampled sites. The hypergeometric subset identity gives u_k as the sum of two exact fractions, independent of overlap. The executable rigorously exhausts all 679 occupancy pairs for n=2..15, tests every strict interior k with Fraction comparisons, and finds sole double-mode case (15,2,9) with peaks (2,7). Direct enumeration of 32768 distinct site subsets under each of disjoint and nested 15-site supports reproduces the full profile independently. A one-species ratio calculation proves unimodality; a binomial-avoidance probability identity proves per-site normalized monotonicity. No infinite extrapolation is asserted.

value.rationale: Exactly-once incidence species are a standard natural rarity component in survey design, and their dependence on sampling depth is not the same as cumulative richness or normalized discovery. Two species are the smallest nontrivial mixture because one species is analytically unimodal; the exhaustive exact result proves 15 sites as the first survey size exhibiting two separate raw-singleton modes and identifies the unique frequency pair at that size. The small 68/5005 secondary-peak-over-trough difference and idealized sampling model substantially limit empirical interpretation but not the mathematical sampling-information boundary.
